extracted.intended_audience: general public; journalists; media organisations; students and researchers interested in press regulation and media ethics in Australia
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting standards, functions and evaluative criteria used by the Australian Press Council for media practice and complaints handling (scope, principles, processes, governance and criticisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of Principles, Specific Standards and Advisory Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council's standards of good media practice are contained in its Statements of Principles, Specific Standards and Advisory Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards are applied by the Council when considering complaints and are used as the basis for statements by Council representatives about good media practice, whether addressing practitioners within the industry, journalism students or the broader community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting high standards of media practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The APC was established with the goal of promoting high standards of media practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an overarching objective informing the Council's activities, including complaint adjudication, statements, research and conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community access to information of public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and protect community access to information of public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Council's remit; standards and actions should not unduly restrict dissemination of information the public needs to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of expression through the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and protect freedom of expression through the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freedom of expression is a fundamental principle used by the Council in adjudications and representations, sometimes invoked to dismiss complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and dealing with complaints about material (print and online)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and deal with complaints and concerns about material in newspapers, magazines and journals, published either in print or on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council handles complaints across platforms; the APC receives more than 700 complaints each year and about three-quarters of fully pursued complaints result in a correction, apology or other action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraging initiatives to address causes of readers' complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage and support initiatives to address the causes for readers' complaints and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes promoting feedback, undertaking research, consultations, convening conferences and seminars, and supporting reforms aimed at preventing repeat issues rather than only punishing individual transgressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and challenging developments that threaten dissemination of public-interest information
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep under review, and where appropriate, challenge developments which may adversely affect the dissemination of information of public interest and may consequently threaten the public's right to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty can lead to representations to governments or public inquiries and policy submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making representations on freedom of speech and access to information
rubrics_metrics.description: Make representations to governments, public inquiries and other forums as appropriate on matters concerning freedom of speech and access to information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council acts as an advocate in policy and public debates about media freedom and information access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of published adjudications and voluntary compliance by publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on the press to voluntarily adhere to the Council's standards of conduct and to publish its adjudications of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The APC has no legal authority to impose fines or penalties; effectiveness depends on publishers' willingness to publish adjudications and take corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction, apology or remedial action as complaint outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrective outcomes — a correction, apology or some other form of action — are common results of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About three-quarters of fully pursued complaints result in such actions, indicating corrective publication outcomes are a key enforcement mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm minimisation principle in journalism ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the 'harm minimisation' principle of journalism ethics and standards when considering complaints (avoid gratuitous harm, stereotyping, calls for violence, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites instances where the Press Council was criticised for overlooking harm minimisation (particularly in complaints about transgender-related material), showing this principle is a substantive standard the Council is expected to uphold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing freedom of expression with harm minimisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance protection of freedom of expression against harm-minimisation obligations when adjudicating complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council has sometimes cited freedom of expression to dismiss complaints even where critics argue harm-minimisation should prevail; this balancing is central to many contested adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency, timeliness and alignment with community expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjudications should be consistent, timely and aligned with community expectations for media standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms from MEAA and others described APC arbitrations as 'inconsistent, slow, and increasingly out of touch with community expectations', indicating these are evaluative metrics for the Council's performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability, sanctions and capacity to censure
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to censure members and provide meaningful consequences when standards are breached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council's lack of legal authority and limited sanctions ('unable to censure its members in anything more than a minor manner') is a recurrent criticism and a key measure of effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination and equal treatment of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure complaints are treated equally regardless of the subject, including vulnerable or protected groups (e.g., transgender people).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal findings (NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal) and recurrent complaints allege the APC treated complaints about transgender subjects less favourably; equal treatment/non-discrimination is therefore a stated expectation and evaluative standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and jurisdiction of the Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandate to consider complaints extends to all print publications and related digital outlets of publishers that are 'constituent bodies' of the Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council covers about 90% of print and online outlets in Australia (some 850 mastheads); jurisdictional coverage and clarity are part of its remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and representativeness of membership and appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Council composition should include independent public members, independent journalists, nominees of media organisations (large and small publishers), and a union nominee, with appointments arranged to preserve independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article describes appointment procedures (Chair appoints public and journalist members; publishers choose their nominees) and raises concerns about industry influence due to publisher-appointed nominees and funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and publication of processes and decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency in Council processes and publication of adjudications and statements on policy matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council issues statements, research and submissions; critics cite publishers ignoring adjudications and breaches of confidentiality as transparency/performance issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research, consultation and education functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake research and consultation on public policy and media developments, and promote understanding of the Council's roles through forums, consultations and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council convenes conferences and seminars, undertakes corpus and other research, and uses findings to inform standards and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliciting and encouraging public feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage feedback for the Council's consideration as part of complaints and standards development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraging feedback is listed among the Council's functions and feeds into policy, standard-setting and adjudication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding independence and conflict-of-interest considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding model (primarily by member publishers, with majority from News Corporation) and its impact on perceived independence and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms emphasize that being funded by the publishers it regulates can compromise the APC's authority and willingness to sanction members; calls for statutory funding or stronger resourcing have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource allocation and strategic priorities (defence vs. proactive engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocation of resources between defending legal proceedings about processes/decisions and proactive engagement with vulnerable groups to improve reporting standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Council reportedly diverted resources to legal defence rather than working with acutely vulnerable transgender groups, a criticism of prioritisation that affects trust and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance frequency and administrative leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Governance arrangements including quarterly meetings, appointment of Chair and Executive Director oversight of administrative matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative rhythm and leadership experience (e.g., Chair's background) are described; governance stability and capability are implicit criteria for institutional performance.
